title: Why lifting is a great hobby for addictive personality types
summary: NH, who has an addictive personality, explains how lifting replaced his video game addiction at 15 when the internet was cut for two months. Lifting suits addictive types because the body forces you to stop before damage is done, and it's the one passion he has never fallen out of in 10 years, unlike football and basketball. The caveat: adding PEDs turns it back into a dangerous addiction.

claims.claim: An addictive personality means getting hooked easily, which is dangerous because moderation matters and toxic substances degrade body or mind.
He has a very addictive personality, evident since age 8-9 and still present at 25: he does something until he's fed up or it consumes him.
Lifting is the perfect hobby for addictive types because your body eventually stops you, unlike binge eating or drugs, where it's too late, or video games, which waste huge amounts of time.
In his MMO phase he played from 8 am to midnight every holiday day for weeks, sometimes forgetting to eat or sleep until he fainted.
Video games are the number one addiction for young men with addictive personalities.
At 15 his internet went out for two months (he suspects his housemates did it on purpose); he started lifting then, and lifting eventually displaced video games entirely.
Addictive types fall out of love with past passions; he lost his obsession with football and then basketball, but lifting has stayed for 10 years and he expects it to last his whole life.
If you get addicted to things you like, give lifting or another sport (powerlifting, strongman) a real shot; it channels obsession into something healthy.
Using lifting to channel an addictive personality only works natural; adding PEDs reactivates the addiction and makes lifting toxic and dangerous.
